Prevention: Destruction of alternate host plants e.g. show flower, okra, brinjal and tomato before sowing.
Eradication of weeds in crop e.g. hazardani and itsit in crop.
Keep the water channels clean from weeds throughout the growing season.
Disinfect agricultural tools/implements after use in mildly hot water for ten minutes.
Monitoring: Monitor alternate host plants initially and later on the crop after two weeks of emergence of the crop twice a week.
Observe very small yellow-coloured nymphs, white waxy adults (females) and white egg sacs attached to the female adults on twigs, on main stem and underside of the leaves.
Be prepared when the temperature is 35-40°C and
RH 60-70% as these favour development of the mealybugs.
Pest scouting can be done any time of the day.
Initially, the attack appears on the edges of the field near water channels and under the shade of the trees.
Do necessary action immediately on the appearance of the pest.
Direct Control: Uproot the infested plants and bury.
Observe the mummified adults (brown to brick red in colour) in the field for the presence of parasitoids ( Aenasius bambawalei ).
Observe the presence of predators (coccinellids and green lacewing).
Avoid application of pesticides when reasonable levels of natural enemies are present in the field.
Restrictions: Tagging and spot spraying with below mentioned pesticides if attack is in patches
Repeat chosen spray after 4 days to control the nymphs hatched from eggs.
Spray in the evening or early morning
Avoid drinking, eating and smoking during the spray
Use safety measures i.e. gloves, cloths, gum boots, masks and goggles while handling and spraying pesticides.
